title: Bound codex-sdk worker runtime timeout
instructions:
Implement only Slice C from references/initiatives/post-review-worker-execution-closure.md. Use that initiative document as read-only source-of-truth for this slice. Slice A and Slice B are already accepted and cleaned; do not reopen them.

Purpose:
- Bound Codex SDK worker runtime execution so a never-ending SDK stream cannot hang the harness.
- Use the workerTimeoutMs input already passed through by Slice B.
- Do not change setup timeout behavior, exec-json timeout behavior, command-runner behavior, worker-result behavior, policy, CLI, lifecycle, cleanup, merge, task templates, or doctrine documents.

Required behavior:
- Bound createCodexSdkWorkerRuntimeAdapter().execute() so thread.runStreamed() and stream consumption return a harness-facing result after workerTimeoutMs.
- On timeout, return runtime command evidence with exitCode 124, timedOut true, timeoutMs, and deterministic timeoutDetails.
- Preserve partial stdout or final response text where available.
- Preserve diagnosable stderr that explains the Codex SDK timeout.
- Preserve thread id and event counts already observed where available.
- Use an SDK abort or cancellation API if one is available in the existing adapter/client shape.
- If safe cancellation is not available, implement the smallest bounded harness-facing result and leave a short code comment stating the limitation. Do not silently ignore timeout.
- Avoid background async work that can keep the harness process alive indefinitely.

Required tests:
- A fake Codex SDK stream that never completes returns a timeout result after workerTimeoutMs.
- The timeout result records exitCode 124, timedOut true, timeoutMs, timeoutDetails, and timeout stderr.
- Partial event counts and thread id are preserved when available.
- Existing SDK success, turn.failed, stream error, and thrown client exception behavior still passes.

Stop conditions:
- Stop and report rework if the SDK timeout path cannot return without leaving the harness process stuck.
- Stop and report rework if the implementation requires worker-owned orchestration or retries.
- Stop and report rework if existing SDK error evidence is lost or made ambiguous.
- Stop and report rework if the implementation requires CLI surface, policy broadening, lifecycle changes, merge/cleanup changes, task template changes, or command-runner changes broader than a narrow helper gap.

Do not edit task templates, docs, lifecycle artifacts, merge/cleanup logic, lesson promotion code, dashboard/daemon/remote behavior, writerCap, hidden memory, Graphify integration, or LLM semantic verification. End with exactly one HARNESS_RESULT line.
